personality.title: How you see yourself
personality.intro: Describe yourself as you usually are, not as you would like to be. There are no right or wrong answers. Your answers are private.

motives.title: What motivates you at work
motives.intro: How much do you agree with each sentence about what is important to you at work?

style.title: How you like to work
style.intro: How much do you agree with each sentence about how you like to work?

pressure.title: You under pressure
pressure.intro: Think about times at work when you were under a lot of pressure, very tired or stressed. How much do you agree with each sentence?

org.title: Your organisation's culture
org.intro: Describe your organisation as it really is in daily work, not how it is described officially.

team.title: Your team's culture
team.intro: Describe your team (or the team you would join) as it really works every day.

criteria.title: Your experience at work
criteria.intro: These questions help us check whether the tool matches real experience. There are no right or wrong answers.

items.text: At social gatherings, I am usually the one who keeps the conversation lively.
I speak very little, even when I am with people I know.
Most of the time, I feel relaxed.
I find it hard to understand ideas that are not practical or concrete.
I can easily picture new things in my mind.
In a group, I prefer to stay quiet and let others take the lead.
When someone is upset, I can understand how they feel.
My work is often careless or untidy.
I rarely feel low or sad.
I am not interested in discussing ideas and theories.
Other people’s problems do not interest me.
I finish my tasks at once, without delay.
After using something, I often forget to put it back in its place.
Small things can upset me easily.
I find it hard to imagine things I have not seen.
At social gatherings, I talk to many different people.
I am not very interested in the lives of other people.
I like to keep my things and my work well organised.
My mood changes many times in a day.
When people around me are happy or sad, I feel it too.
I want people to praise my achievements.
I want a job where my decisions affect the results.
Having fun at work is important to me.
I want my work to help other people.
Working closely with a friendly team is important to me.
I respect the traditions and established ways of my organisation.
A stable, secure job is very important to me.
A good salary is one of the main things I look for in a job.
I care a lot about how good my work looks and how well it is made.
I like decisions to be based on facts and data.
I want senior people to see what I contribute.
I enjoy leading people and directing their work.
I like a lively, friendly workplace with lots of humour.
Helping colleagues learn and grow makes me happy.
I prefer a job where I work closely with colleagues for most of the day.
Clear rules of behaviour and respect for senior people are important to me.
I avoid career moves that are very uncertain.
I watch closely how much money my work earns or saves.
Good design and careful work motivate me.
I am motivated by understanding how things work in detail.
To show you are reading carefully, please choose "Agree" here.
I like to decide quickly and change things later if needed.
I am comfortable acting when I do not know what will happen.
I say openly when I disagree, even with senior people.
I work best when I can decide how to do my work.
Slow review and approval processes annoy me.
I prefer to try a bold idea rather than a safe one.
Open discussion, even with disagreement, leads to better decisions.
When my manager checks my work very closely, I feel less motivated.
I work best where colleagues know each other well and help each other without being asked.
I work best where I can try new, untested ideas, and a failed idea is seen as a chance to learn.
I work best where I know my targets and how my results compare with others.
I work best where it is clear who makes which decisions and how work should be done.
I work best where plans change quickly when a good new opportunity appears.
I work best where pay and promotion depend mainly on measurable results.
I work best where people are asked for their opinion before decisions that affect them.
I work best where rules are applied in the same way to everyone, every time.
When I am under pressure, I can get angry or emotional.
When I am under pressure, I start to distrust other people’s intentions.
When I am under pressure, I avoid making decisions in case they are wrong.
When I am under pressure, I trust my own opinion more than other people’s advice.
When I am under pressure, I sometimes ignore rules to get things done.
When I am under pressure, I find it hard to give work to others, because they may not do it well enough.
When I am under pressure, I want my manager to make the difficult decisions.
When I am under pressure, I lose patience with people or projects quickly.
When I am under pressure, I wonder whether others are being honest with me.
When I am under pressure, I wait for more information before I decide, even when time is short.
When I am under pressure, I find it hard to admit I was wrong.
When I am under pressure, I take shortcuts that others may see as risky.
When I am under pressure, I focus too much on details and check my work again and again.
When I am under pressure, I agree with senior people even when I have doubts.
To check quality, please choose "Agree" here.

In my organisation, people can try new, untested ideas, and a failed idea is seen as a chance to learn.
In my organisation, everyone knows their targets and how their results compare with others.

Senior leaders say that people come first and everyone should work as one team.
Senior leaders say the organisation should be innovative, fast and willing to take smart risks.
Senior leaders say the organisation should focus on reaching targets and beating competitors.
Senior leaders say the organisation should be disciplined, control costs and follow good processes.
In my organisation, decisions are made quickly.
In my organisation, people are encouraged to take sensible risks.
In my organisation, people can disagree openly, even with senior leaders.
In my organisation, people are free to decide how to do their work.
In my organisation, decisions need approval from many levels.
In my organisation, mistakes are punished.
In my organisation, people avoid speaking up about problems.
In my organisation, managers check people’s work very closely.
In my organisation, people feel safe to admit mistakes and ask for help.
In my organisation, senior leaders keep their promises.
I would tell a friend that my organisation is a great place to work.
In my organisation, people are afraid to speak up.

In my team, people can try new, untested ideas, and a failed idea is seen as a chance to learn.

In my team, people are free to decide how to do their work.
My personal values are similar to my organisation’s values.
I fit in well with my team’s way of working.
Overall, I am satisfied with my job.

changelog: FC-1.1: culture items (CP, OR, TC, OE) reworded as concrete, original behavioural statements to keep clear of the wording of proprietary culture instruments. Do not pool these items with FC-1.0 pilot data.

FC-1.2: every item, answer label and block introduction rewritten in plain English (short sentences, common words, no idioms) for non-native speakers. The IPIP-50 items are a plain-English adaptation with the same content and keying; confirm reliability and convergent validity before comparing with published IPIP norms.

FC-2.0 short form: 179 → 115 items. Personality = Mini-IPIP 20; two strongest items per motive, style and pressure scale; culture items use identical content for self, team and organisation; ESL recalibration of personality stems for Indian professionals. Not comparable item-for-item with FC-1.x.
